Doro.content: DM: Session 2 - the Salt Mother. The harbourmaster blames you for the broken lens and demands you "fix what you broke". Buck, who learned the coastal script, can now read the rest of the keeper's logbook: the Salt Mother is a sea hag who lives in the drowned chapel under the reef, and the keeper traded her the lighthouse's light for his drowned daughter's return. At low tide you wade into the drowned chapel: knee-deep water, barnacled pews, candles burning underwater. The sea-chest from the lighthouse (you hauled it here - Pim never opened it) starts to knock from the inside. A voice from the altar, sweet as honey: "Little thieves. Bring me my light, or bring me one of you." What do you do?

"By Moradin's Forge, we've stumbled into a right mess. Ione, lend me your wisdom—what do you know of hag's bargains?" I Raise a Shield, then Stride, then Strike the sea-chest with my warhammer, [Strength] to damage it. "If it's a fight she wants, let's give her a taste of steel!" [Champion's Devotion] for a boon, [Religion] to see if the light can be used against her.

DM (results): Doro's Champion's Devotion works (Religion 23): a warm glow, +1 to his next save - but his hammer glances off the iron-bound chest. Ione taps back on the chest and it answers (Diplomacy 21): a little girl's voice - Maris, the keeper's drowned daughter, trapped inside as a child made of seawater. Pim's untrained peek goes badly (crit fail, a face full of brine), and he then slings the chest across the water - straight onto the Salt Mother's altar (unnoticed, 18). Glafka's light finds nothing (11). Buck's leap onto the altar falls short (14) and he splashes down; a barnacled hand rises from the water and he arm-wrestles it - and loses by ONE (23 vs 24): the hand drags him under. Kestrel's arrow hits something at the altar (8): the Salt Mother rises, a sea hag draped in kelp, the chest now under her claw. Two drowned sailors lurch out of the pews. FIGHT, round 1 (3 actions each). What do you do?

"By the Anvil, I won't let that foul hag claim another soul!" I Raise a Shield, then Stride to Buck's last position, then Strike at the barnacled hand dragging him under, [Strength] to damage it. "Retributive Strike!" if it hits, [Constitution] to resist the pull. "Kestrel, keep that hag busy! Ione, can you dispel her kelp cloak? Pim, anything you can open or pick that chest?" I'm also trying to make sure Buck doesn't drown, [Acrobatics] to keep my balance in the knee-deep water.

DM (results): Doro's hammer is a NAT 1 - it smashes a pew instead - but the hag's claw at him is a NAT 1 too and rakes only water. Pim's Improvised Blinding lands (21): a fistful of salt and the hag shrieks, blinded, and Pim swims to Buck (14). Buck, underwater: his water-ballet flip is a NAT 1, the flying kick misses, the wall run slides off the wet stone - three failures - but he holds his breath (Fort 24) and bobs up spluttering. Kestrel's Salt-Wind Shot hits the hag (25, 7); the second arrow misses. Ione begs the hag to free Maris and is laughed at (crit fail); her cantrip misses and a drowned sailor hits her for 10. The blinded hag clutches the chest to her chest: "Take her, then, and the sea takes you." Round 2 - last round. What do you do?

"By my oath, I won't let that creature win!" I Raise a Shield, then Stride to the hag's position, then Strike at the chest with my warhammer, [Strength] to damage it and free Maris. "Shield Block!" if the hag attacks, [Reaction] to reduce the damage. "Kestrel, keep her blinded! Pim, Buck, get Ione to safety!" I'm also trying to use the barnacled pews as cover, [Athletics] to climb onto one and get a better angle at the chest. "Champion's Devotion!" for a boon, [Religion] to see if I can turn the light against the hag if I free Maris.

DM (results): Doro's hammer crits the chest's lock (27) and Buck - NAT 20 - tears the lid wide open even as he fails to pull the chest away from the hag and takes a claw (6). A wave of seawater pours out and stands up as a little girl: Maris. Ione's fire spell scorches the blinded hag (13) and she shoves the drowned sailor off her; the hag shrieks, lets go, and dissolves into the tide, fleeing. Pim tries to tow Ione to shore and it's a NAT 1 - both go under and come up coughing. Kestrel's arrow at the chest misses (16). Maris is flesh again by dawn; the keeper's ghost is at peace; Brinemouth forgives the lens - mostly.
DOWNTIME: a week in Brinemouth while the glassworks casts a new lens (the town pays half, you owe the rest). There's the glassworks, the fish market, Gozreh's temple, the tavern's arm-wrestling table, the scholar, Maris and her grandmother, and a regatta on the last day. What does your character spend the week doing? Give 2-3 things.

"By the Forge, we've earned a rest, but I won't idle while there's work to be done." I spend the week training with my shield and warhammer in Gozreh's temple courtyard, [Athletics] to improve my prowess and honor the goddess of the sea. I also volunteer at the fish market, using my strength to help unload and organize the catch, [Diplomacy] to build goodwill with the townsfolk and learn more about their culture. Finally, I visit the scholar to learn more about the Salt Mother and other local threats, [Arcana] to deepen my understanding of the supernatural. "And if there's time, I'll challenge someone to an arm-wrestling match at the tavern!"
